UK-GDPR-13-1-e.instrument: UK GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as retained in UK law)
UK-GDPR-13-1-e.title: Recipients must be disclosed
UK-GDPR-13-1-e.summary: When collecting data, the controller must tell the person the recipients or categories of recipients of the personal data.

UK-GDPR-5-1-a.instrument: UK GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as retained in UK law)
UK-GDPR-5-1-a.title: Lawfulness, fairness and transparency
UK-GDPR-5-1-a.summary: Personal data must be processed lawfully, fairly and in a transparent manner in relation to the data subject.

UK-GDPR-13-1-c.instrument: UK GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as retained in UK law)
UK-GDPR-13-1-c.title: Purposes and legal basis must be disclosed
UK-GDPR-13-1-c.summary: When collecting data from the person, the controller must state the purposes of the processing and its legal basis.

UK-GDPR-28.instrument: UK GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as retained in UK law)
UK-GDPR-28.title: Processors
UK-GDPR-28.summary: A controller may only use processors that provide sufficient guarantees, under a contract that sets out the processing.

UK-PECR-6.instrument: Privacy and Electronic Communications (EC Directive) Regulations 2003 (PECR)
UK-PECR-6.ref: reg. 6(1), as substituted by Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 s. 112
UK-PECR-6.title: Storing or accessing information on a user's device
UK-PECR-6.summary: A person must not store information, or gain access to information stored, in a user's terminal equipment unless an exception in Schedule A1 applies (for example consent, or strict necessity).

UK-PECR-SCHA1-5.instrument: PECR Schedule A1, inserted by Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 Sch. 12
UK-PECR-SCHA1-5.title: Statistical-purposes exception for analytics cookies
UK-PECR-SCHA1-5.summary: Consent is not required where storage or access is solely to collect statistical information about how a service or website is used, with a view to improving it, provided the user is given clear information and a simple means to object. Advertising and cross-site tracking are outside the exception.

UK-GDPR-13-1-f.instrument: UK GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as retained in UK law)
UK-GDPR-13-1-f.title: International transfers must be disclosed
UK-GDPR-13-1-f.summary: The controller must tell the person if it intends to transfer personal data to a third country or international organisation, and the safeguards relied on.

UK-GDPR-44.instrument: UK GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as retained in UK law)
UK-GDPR-44.title: General principle for transfers
UK-GDPR-44.summary: Personal data may be transferred outside the UK only if the conditions of Chapter V are met.

UK-GDPR-17.instrument: UK GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as retained in UK law)
UK-GDPR-17.title: Right to erasure
UK-GDPR-17.summary: The person has the right to have personal data erased without undue delay in listed cases.

UK-GDPR-5-1-f.instrument: UK GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as retained in UK law)
UK-GDPR-5-1-f.title: Integrity and confidentiality
UK-GDPR-5-1-f.summary: Personal data must be processed with appropriate security, including protection against unauthorised access.

UK-GDPR-5-1-e.instrument: UK GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as retained in UK law)
UK-GDPR-5-1-e.title: Storage limitation
UK-GDPR-5-1-e.summary: Personal data must be kept in identifiable form no longer than necessary for the purposes for which it is processed.

UK-GDPR-13-2-a.instrument: UK GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as retained in UK law)
UK-GDPR-13-2-a.title: Retention period must be stated
UK-GDPR-13-2-a.summary: The controller must state the period for which personal data will be stored or the criteria used to determine that period.

UK-ICO-AI-GUIDANCE.instrument: ICO Guidance on AI and data protection (regulator guidance, not statute)
UK-ICO-AI-GUIDANCE.title: Be transparent about AI processing of personal data
UK-ICO-AI-GUIDANCE.summary: The UK has no AI-specific statute. ICO guidance expects organisations to tell people when and how their personal data is processed by AI systems, as part of UK GDPR transparency. Guidance only, so status is capped at amber.

UK-DMCC-227.instrument: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, Part 4 Chapter 1
UK-DMCC-227.title: Misleading omissions
UK-DMCC-227.summary: A practice involves a misleading omission if it omits or hides material information the average consumer needs to take an informed transactional decision.

UK-DMCC-226.instrument: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, Part 4 Chapter 1
UK-DMCC-226.title: Misleading actions
UK-DMCC-226.summary: A practice involves a misleading action if it provides false or misleading information relating to the product or trader and is likely to cause the average consumer to take a transactional decision they would not otherwise take.

UK-DMCC-225.instrument: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, Part 4 Chapter 1
UK-DMCC-225.title: Prohibition of unfair commercial practices
UK-DMCC-225.summary: Unfair commercial practices are prohibited, including misleading actions, misleading omissions and practices that contravene professional diligence.

EU-GDPR-5-1-a.title: Lawfulness, fairness and transparency
EU-GDPR-5-1-a.summary: Personal data must be processed lawfully, fairly and in a transparent manner in relation to the data subject. A policy statement that contradicts actual processing is hard to square with transparency.

EU-GDPR-13-1-e.title: Recipients must be disclosed
EU-GDPR-13-1-e.summary: When collecting data, the controller must tell the person the recipients or categories of recipients of the personal data.

EU-GDPR-13-1-c.title: Purposes and legal basis must be disclosed
EU-GDPR-13-1-c.summary: When collecting data from the person, the controller must state the purposes of the processing and its legal basis.

EU-EPRIVACY-5-3.title: Consent for cookies and similar technologies
EU-EPRIVACY-5-3.summary: Storing information, or accessing information stored, on a user's device is only allowed with the user's consent after clear information, unless strictly necessary to provide a service the user requested. There is no exemption for analytics.

EU-GDPR-7.title: Conditions for consent
EU-GDPR-7.summary: Where processing relies on consent, the controller must be able to demonstrate that the person consented, and consent must be as easy to withdraw as to give.

EU-GDPR-6.title: Lawful basis for processing
EU-GDPR-6.summary: Processing is lawful only if at least one legal basis applies, such as consent, contract, legal obligation or legitimate interests.

EU-GDPR-28.title: Processors
EU-GDPR-28.summary: A controller may only use processors that provide sufficient guarantees, under a contract that sets out the subject matter, duration, nature and purpose of the processing.

EU-GDPR-13-1-f.title: Third-country transfers must be disclosed
EU-GDPR-13-1-f.summary: The controller must tell the person if it intends to transfer personal data to a third country, and reference the adequacy decision or safeguards relied on.

EU-GDPR-44.title: General principle for transfers
EU-GDPR-44.summary: Personal data may be transferred to a third country only if the conditions of Chapter V (adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards) are met.

EU-GDPR-17.title: Right to erasure
EU-GDPR-17.summary: The person has the right to have personal data erased without undue delay in listed cases, for example when it is no longer necessary or consent is withdrawn.

EU-GDPR-13-2-b.title: Data subject rights must be listed
EU-GDPR-13-2-b.summary: The controller must inform the person of the rights to access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and data portability.

EU-GDPR-5-1-f.title: Integrity and confidentiality
EU-GDPR-5-1-f.summary: Personal data must be processed with appropriate security, including protection against unauthorised access. Personal data written to application logs widens who can access it.

EU-GDPR-5-1-e.title: Storage limitation
EU-GDPR-5-1-e.summary: Personal data must be kept in identifiable form no longer than necessary for the purposes for which it is processed.

EU-GDPR-13-2-a.title: Retention period must be stated
EU-GDPR-13-2-a.summary: The controller must state the period for which personal data will be stored or, if that is not possible, the criteria used to determine that period.

EU-AIACT-50-1.title: People must be told they are interacting with an AI system
EU-AIACT-50-1.summary: Providers must ensure AI systems intended to interact directly with people are designed so that people are informed they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the context.

EU-UCPD-6.title: Misleading actions
EU-UCPD-6.summary: A practice is misleading if it contains false information, or is likely to deceive the average consumer, and causes a transactional decision the consumer would not otherwise have taken.

EU-UCPD-7.title: Misleading omissions
EU-UCPD-7.summary: A practice is misleading if it omits or hides material information that the average consumer needs to take an informed transactional decision.

EU-UCPD-5.title: Prohibition of unfair commercial practices
EU-UCPD-5.summary: Unfair commercial practices are prohibited: practices contrary to professional diligence that materially distort the economic behaviour of the average consumer.

KZ-PD-7.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V 'On Personal Data and their Protection' (21 May 2013)
KZ-PD-7.title: Conditions for collection and processing
KZ-PD-7.summary: Collection and processing of personal data is carried out with the consent of the subject, except in cases set by law. Transfer to third parties and cross-border transfer are subject to consent.

KZ-PD-8.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V 'On Personal Data and their Protection' (21 May 2013)
KZ-PD-8.title: Required content of consent
KZ-PD-8.summary: Consent must state, among other things, its validity period, whether data may be transferred to third parties, whether cross-border transfer takes place, and the list of data collected.

KZ-PD-12-2.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V 'On Personal Data and their Protection' (21 May 2013)
KZ-PD-12-2.title: Storage in Kazakhstan and retention period
KZ-PD-12-2.summary: Personal data must be stored in a database or digital facility located in the territory of Kazakhstan. The retention period is set by the date the purposes of collection and processing are achieved.

KZ-PD-16.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V 'On Personal Data and their Protection' (21 May 2013)
KZ-PD-16.title: Cross-border transfer
KZ-PD-16.summary: Cross-border transfer is allowed only to states that ensure protection of personal data, or otherwise on limited grounds such as the subject's consent to the cross-border transfer.

KZ-PD-25.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V 'On Personal Data and their Protection' (21 May 2013)
KZ-PD-25.title: Duties of the owner and operator
KZ-PD-25.summary: The owner or operator must take legal, organisational and technical measures to protect personal data, be able to evidence consent, give the subject access to their data, and destroy data in the cases set by law.

KZ-PD-24.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V 'On Personal Data and their Protection' (21 May 2013)
KZ-PD-24.title: Rights of the subject
KZ-PD-24.summary: The subject has rights including to know what personal data the owner or operator holds, to require changes, blocking and destruction of data in cases set by law, and to withdraw consent.

KZ-AI-16.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII 'On Artificial Intelligence' (17 November 2025, in force 18 January 2026)
KZ-AI-16.title: User rights when interacting with AI systems
KZ-AI-16.summary: Users have the right to read the user agreement of the AI system, to protection of their personal data processed by it, to explanations of results affecting their rights, and to refuse to interact with an AI system where interaction is not mandatory by law.

KZ-AI-21-1.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 230-VIII 'On Artificial Intelligence' (17 November 2025, in force 18 January 2026)
KZ-AI-21-1.title: Users must be informed that AI is used
KZ-AI-21-1.summary: Users must be informed that goods, works and services are produced or provided using artificial intelligence systems.

KZ-CP-10.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 274-IV 'On Protection of Consumer Rights' (4 May 2010)
KZ-CP-10.title: Consumer right to information
KZ-CP-10.summary: The consumer has the right to receive full, reliable and timely information about goods, works and services and about the seller or provider.

KZ-CP-25.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 274-IV 'On Protection of Consumer Rights' (4 May 2010)
KZ-CP-25.title: Seller's duty to provide information
KZ-CP-25.summary: The seller or provider must give the consumer the mandatory information about the goods, works or services, including their main consumer properties.
